introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the experimental set up you would use. *[4 marks]*

$25\ \text{cm}^3$ of 0.25M NaOH was transferred into a conical flask and 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator were added.

(i) Name the apparatus used to transfer the NaOH solution.

(ii) State the colour change in the conical flask.
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **$25\ \text{cm}^3$ pipette** (with a pipette filler).

(ii) Phenolphthalein is **colourless in acid and pink in alkali**, so when the drops are added to the NaOH solution the flask contents change from **colourless to pink**.

The dilute acid was run from the burette and two accurate results were recorded as shown on the following diagrams:

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(i) Read and record the results of experiment 1 and 2 on the following table. *[3 marks]*

| | Experiment 1 | Experiment 2 |
|---|---|---|
| final reading |  |  |
| initial reading |  |  |
| Titre |  |  |

(ii) Determine the mean titre of the dilute hydrochloride acid used. *[1 mark]*

(iii) What will be the colour change to indicate the end of the experiment? *[1 mark]*

(iv) Calculate the concentration of the dilute HCl(aq) solution if $25\ \text{cm}^3$ of 0.25M NaOH was required.

(v) In carrying out this experiment the acid accidentally spilled on the student's hands. Advice the student on what should be done. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Burette readings are taken at the bottom of the meniscus, to $0.1\ \text{cm}^3$ (each small division is $0.1\ \text{cm}^3$):

| | Experiment 1 | Experiment 2 |
|---|---|---|
| final reading | 16.2 | 26.3 |
| initial reading | 0.1 | 10.2 |
| Titre | 16.1 | 16.1 |

(units: $\text{cm}^3$; titre = final reading - initial reading).

(ii) Mean titre $= \dfrac{16.1 + 16.1}{2} = \mathbf{16.1\ cm^3}$.

(iii) Phenolphthalein is pink in alkali and colourless in acid, so the end point is the **change from pink to colourless** (one drop of acid removes the last trace of pink).

(iv) Equation: $\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ (1 mole of NaOH reacts with 1 mole of HCl).

Moles of NaOH $= 0.25\times\dfrac{25}{1000} = 0.00625$ mol, so moles of HCl in the mean titre $= 0.00625$ mol.

Concentration of HCl $= \dfrac{0.00625}{16.1/1000} = 0.388\ \text{mol dm}^{-3} \approx \mathbf{0.39\ M}$.

(v) **Wash the hands immediately and thoroughly with plenty of running water** (for several minutes), then tell the teacher, and seek medical attention if the skin still burns or is red.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following graph was drawn by a student using result obtained for the reaction between Zinc and dilute HCl(aq).

![fig-2](gce-ol-chemistry-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

(i) In two separate experiments Zinc granules and powdered zinc were used simultaneously. Which curve represents result from the use of granulated zinc? ... Powdered zinc: ...

(ii) Using your graph, determine the total volume of hydrogen gas collected at the end of the reaction. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Powdered zinc: curve a. Granulated zinc: curve b.** Curve a is steeper, so the reaction is faster: powdered zinc has a much larger surface area exposed to the acid, so more collisions per second occur. The reaction with granules is slower (curve b).

(ii) Both curves level off at the same height, because the same amount of zinc and acid react and the same total volume of gas is produced. Reading the plateau on the graph: **about $89\ \text{cm}^3$ of hydrogen** (the line lies just under the $90\ \text{cm}^3$ mark; $88$ to $90\ \text{cm}^3$ is acceptable).
